subject: Springboard throughput escalation: RCA delivery & exec commitments
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@springboard.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara@springboard.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: urgent: throughput drop and increased 500s during peak window

David —

We observed a ~60% drop in throughput for inference requests to model-redwood-7b between 07:10–08:05 PT this morning; error rate (5xx) spiked from ~0.4% to 6.8% and tail latency jumped to ~1.4s P95 (usual ~220ms). This impacted our checkout flow for a ~45-minute window and caused multiple timeouts in our background workers.

Attached are our logs and a short sample trace. Can we get an initial RCA and an ETA for a permanent fix? Our procurement and exec teams are copying in procurement@springboard.ai — they need an incident summary for their post-mortem and any SLA implications.

Attachments: springboard_client_logs_20270602.zip (attachment stub), sample-trace.txt (attachment stub)

Alex
Head of Platform — Springboard.ai
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@springboard.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: urgent: throughput drop and increased 500s during peak window

Alex —

Thanks for the data and the heads-up. I'm standing up an incident bridge now and have looped in Jonas (serving runtime lead) and Marissa (customer success). We'll triage immediately and share a concise RCA within 24 hours, plus a short-term mitigation plan to restore throughput while we validate the root cause.

Immediate asks for you so we can triage faster:
- Can you confirm the exact model variant (quantized vs. FP16) and the typical sequence length distribution for the impacted requests?
- Any recent config changes on your side (prompt engineering, batch size, concurrency) in the 24 hours prior to the spike?

I'll post the bridge notes and link to our incident ticket in the thread ASAP.

-David
David Kim
VP, Customer Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@springboard.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: urgent: throughput drop and increased 500s during peak window

Bridge summary and preliminary findings:

Summary (prelim)
- Root cause signal: a cascading KV-cache eviction behavior on our serving tier when a burst of long-sequence warmup requests coincided with autoscaler ramp-down. The combination caused excessive KV cache churn, causing stalls and an elevated error rate from resource thrashing.
- Impact window: 07:10–08:05 PT (matches customer traces).
- Immediate mitigations applied (07:40 PT): temporarily pinned a higher cache retention policy for Springboard's live pool; increased worker concurrency on the affected cluster; disabled aggressive autoscaler scale-in for 20m. These brought error rate back under 1% by 07:58 PT and recovered throughput gradually.

Evidence attached: automated KV eviction logs, kernel selection timeline, sample trace correlation (see attachment: kv-cache-analysis.csv).

Next steps (owners & ETA)
- Short-term (24–72h): deploy configuration change to default cache retention and add a customer-scoped override to avoid future churn spikes (owner: Jonas Weber; ETA: 48h).
- Medium-term (2–3 weeks): refine autoscaler policy to consider active KV cache footprint (owner: Runtime team; ETA: 3 weeks).
- Validation: run a canary with Springboard's production workload during off-peak to prove fix (owner: Marissa Cole + Springboard engineers; ETA: scheduled by 06/03).

I'll attach a short mitigation runbook and a concise RCA PDF for your execs.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
Attachments: kv-cache-analysis.csv (attachment stub), mitigation_runbook.md (attachment stub), springboard_rca_v1.pdf (attachment stub)

Subject: Re: urgent: throughput drop and increased 500s during peak window — canary and exec readout planning

Marissa/David —

Appreciate the quick triage and the canary schedule. A few asks from our side:
- Please include an explicit SLA credit calculation in the EOD readout — procurement wants the formal numbers and the timeframe used for the calculation.
- We'd like an exec-level bridge on 06/04 09:00 PT to confirm the permanent mitigation timeline; our CTO will join.
- For goodwill, please propose a small credit (we lost orders during the window) — we can discuss numbers on the bridge.

We ran the canary in the morning and prelim signals look good — error rate stayed <0.8% for the test batches. We'll share the final canary logs shortly.

Thanks,
Alex
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@springboard.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@springboard.ai
Date: 2027-06-04T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Final: RCA delivered, ownership & commitments (action tracker)

Alex/Tara —

Thank you again for the partnership and patience. This message consolidates the final RCA and our commitments following the canary validation. Attached: springboard_rca_v1.pdf (executive-friendly 1-pager), mitigation_runbook.md, and the KV cache traces.

Final summary (concise)
- Cause: KV-cache eviction churn combined with autoscaler scale-in during a burst of long-sequence requests -> resource thrash -> elevated 5xx and tail latency.
- Short-term remediation (completed): pinned cache retention + temporary scale-in hold. Canary (06/03) validated recovery profile.
- Medium-term remediation (committed): autoscaler policy change to consider KV footprint + telemetry to detect early churn (owner: Runtime / Jonas; ETA: 2027-06-25).
- Compensation: Redwood proposes a usage credit equivalent to one week of average token spend during the impacted service window (proposal sent to procurement@springboard.ai; open to discussion on the 06/04 exec bridge).

Action tracker (owner — task — due)
- Jonas Weber — push autoscaler policy update and config tests — due 2027-06-25 — ticket: INF-2138.
- Marissa Cole — coordinate production canary with Springboard validation and collect canary logs — due 2027-06-05 — link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/SPRINGBOARD-RCA-DOC.
- Karthik Iyer — own customer follow-up and billing/credit negotiation — due 2027-06-07.
- David Kim — exec bridge & approval for compensation proposal — scheduled 2027-06-04 09:00 PT.

We'll keep the incident ticket open until the autoscaler policy is deployed and validated. Please reply to this thread with any gaps or if you need expanded documentation.

-David Kim
VP, Customer Engineering — Redwood Inference
